name: Clocks
intro: **One formula does almost everything: angle = |30H − 5.5M|.** The hour hand moves 0.5°/min and the minute hand 6°/min, and 30H − 5.5M is just the difference (§2).
If the formula returns more than 180°, subtract from 360° to get the smaller angle — unless the question explicitly asks for the reflex angle.

qs.q: Find the angle (in degrees) between the hands of a clock at 3:20.
qs.h: §2 — |30(3) − 5.5(20)|. The common wrong answer of 0° assumes the hour hand stays on the 3.

qs.q: The angle between the hands at 4:40 is
Find the angle (in degrees) between the hands at 7:10.
qs.h: §2 — |210 − 55|. Still under 180, so no correction is needed.

qs.q: The angle between the hands at 9:30 is
qs.h: §2 — the hour hand is halfway between 9 and 10, not on the 9.

qs.q: Find the reflex angle (in degrees) between the hands at 2:50.
qs.h: §2 — the formula gives 215°, which is already the reflex angle; the smaller one is 145°. Read which is wanted.
qs.s: |60 − 275| = 215° ⟹ the reflex angle is 215° (the smaller angle being 145°).

qs.q: At what time between 3 and 4 o'clock do the hands coincide? Give the number of minutes past 3, to two decimals.
qs.h: §3 — coincidence means the angle is 0, so 30H = 5.5M.

qs.q: Between 2 and 3 o'clock, the hands point in exactly opposite directions at
qs.h: §3 — opposition means an angle of 180°, so solve |60 − 5.5M| = 180.

qs.q: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock are the hands first at right angles? Give minutes past 4, to two decimals.
qs.h: §4 — solve |120 − 5.5M| = 90. There are two solutions in the hour; the question wants the earlier.
qs.s: 5.5M = 30 ⟹ M = 5.45 (the other right angle falls at 38.18 minutes past 4).

qs.q: How many times in 12 hours do the hands of a clock coincide?
qs.h: §3 — between 11 and 1 there is only one coincidence, at 12 o'clock. That is what costs the twelfth.
qs.s: 11 times — once in each hour except that the 11 o'clock and 12 o'clock cases are the same event.

qs.q: How many times in 24 hours are the hands of a clock at right angles?
qs.h: §3 — 22 in 12 hours, by the same logic that gives 11 coincidences.
qs.s: 22 per 12 hours ⟹ 44 times in a day.

qs.q: A clock gains 5 minutes every hour. If it is set right at 8 a.m., how many minutes will it be ahead at 8 p.m. the same day?
qs.h: §5 — a uniform gain accumulates linearly over the elapsed hours.

qs.q: A clock gains 10 seconds per hour and is set right at 6 a.m. At the true time of 6 p.m. the same day, it shows
qs.h: §5 — convert the total gain into minutes at the end.

qs.q: A clock is set right at 5 a.m. and loses 16 minutes in 24 hours. When the clock shows 10 p.m. on the fourth day, how many minutes past 10 p.m. is the true time?
qs.h: §5 — the clock shows 1424 minutes for every 1440 true minutes, so scale the shown interval up by 1440/1424.
qs.s: Shown interval = 89 hours = 5340 min ⟹ true = 5340 × 1440/1424 = 5400 min = 90 hours ⟹ true time is 11 p.m., i.e. 60 minutes past 10 p.m.

qs.q: Two clocks are set right at noon. One gains 2 minutes a day and the other loses 3 minutes a day. They will be 1 hour apart after
qs.h: §5 — the gap grows at the sum of the two rates, since they drift in opposite directions.

qs.q: A watch gains uniformly. It was 3 minutes slow at noon on Monday and 3 minutes fast at 9 p.m. the following Monday. How many hours after noon on Monday did it show the correct time?
qs.h: §5 — the total drift is 6 minutes over the whole interval; the correct moment is where half of it has accumulated.
qs.s: Interval = 7 days 9 hours = 177 hours for a 6-minute swing ⟹ correct at 177 × 3/6 = 88.5 hours after noon on Monday.

sets.name: Mirror images and counting within a window

qs.q: A clock seen in a mirror appears to show 8:20. The actual time is
qs.h: §6 — subtract the shown time from 11:60 (i.e. 12:00), which is the reflection rule for any time other than exactly 12.

qs.q: The mirror image of a clock shows 2:30. Express the actual time as the number of minutes past 9.
qs.h: §6 — the same subtraction; here it lands on a whole half-hour.

qs.q: A clock in a mirror appears to show 10:10. The actual time is
qs.h: §6 — 11:60 minus the shown time.

qs.q: How many times between 3 p.m. and 9 p.m. do the hands of a clock coincide?
qs.h: §7 — coincidences recur every 720/11 minutes; count how many land inside the window.

qs.q: After the hands of a clock coincide, they next coincide after
qs.h: §3 — 11 coincidences spread over 12 hours.

qs.q: Find the angle (in degrees) between the hands at 5:30.
qs.h: The hour hand is halfway to 6.

qs.q: The angle between the hands at 8:24 is
At what time between 6 and 7 o'clock do the hands coincide? Give minutes past 6, to two decimals.
How many times in 24 hours do the hands of a clock point in opposite directions?
qs.h: 11 per 12 hours, for the same reason as coincidences.

qs.q: A clock gains 4 minutes every hour and is set right at 9 a.m. How many minutes past 9 p.m. does it show at the true time of 9 p.m. the same day?
qs.h: Linear accumulation over 12 hours.

qs.q: A clock seen in a mirror shows 4:35. The actual time is
qs.h: 11:60 minus the shown time.

qs.q: At what time between 10 and 11 o'clock are the hands at right angles for the second time? Give minutes past 10, to two decimals.
qs.h: Two solutions: 300 − 5.5M = 270 and 300 − 5.5M = 90. Take the later one.
qs.s: 5.5M = 210 ⟹ M = 38.18 (the first right angle was at 5.45 minutes past 10).

qs.q: A clock loses 5 minutes every hour and is set right at 6 a.m. At the true time of 6 p.m. the same day, it shows
qs.h: 12 hours of loss at 5 minutes an hour.

audit: treating the hour hand as fixed on the hour mark instead of advancing 0.5° per minute (§2)
A5
reporting the smaller angle where the reflex angle was asked, or vice versa
using 6M instead of 5.5M — the relative speed of the hands is 5.5°/min, not 6 (§3)
B3, M7
finding only one of the two right angles in an hour, or picking the wrong one (§4)
answering 12 or 24 by assuming one event per hour (§3)
mixing the units of the drift, or applying it to the wrong number of hours (§5)
C3
scaling the shown interval down instead of up for a slow clock
C4
subtracting the two drift rates when the clocks drift in opposite directions
subtracting from 12:00 without borrowing correctly — use 11:60 (§6)
D4, D5
assuming coincidences fall exactly one hour apart rather than 65.45 minutes (§7)
